reversal_steps: Delete the report from the compliance management system if generated in error
reversal_basis: Compliance reports are documents generated by SIEM/compliance tools. Generating a report is read-only with respect to system configuration. The report itself can be deleted or retracted. Creates no change to the security posture.
source_reference: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.4 Post-Incident Activity | ISO 27001:2022 A.5.25
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — report generation is a documentation/audit action

reversal_steps: ⚠️ THIS ACTION REQUIRES HUMAN APPROVAL AND CANNOT BE AUTO-EXECUTED
Check SIEM long-term storage or WORM storage for log backup
Restore from centralized log archive (Splunk, Elastic, Glacier, Cloudwatch Logs)
reversal_basis: Audit log deletion is a high-risk, potentially irreversible action that undermines forensic investigation capability and triggers compliance violations (PCI 10.5.1, HIPAA §164.312(b), NIST AU-9). Deleted logs may be recoverable from SIEM/WORM archives only if pre-configured. This action MUST NEVER be auto-executed — always routes to L1/L2 analyst queue for manual approval regardless of context.
source_reference: PCI-DSS v4 10.5.1 | NIST 800-53 AU-9 (Protection of Audit Information) | HIPAA §164.312(b) | ISO 27001 A.8.15 — https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/sp/800-53/rev-5/final
risk_if_not_reversed: Permanent loss of forensic evidence — potential compliance violation across all frameworks (PCI, HIPAA, GDPR, NIST, ISO 27001). Chain of custody broken.

reversal_steps: ⚠️ THIS ACTION REQUIRES HUMAN APPROVAL AND CANNOT BE AUTO-EXECUTED
Re-enable MFA via IdP admin console (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace)
Or re-enforce MFA via IAM policy on the affected account
reversal_basis: Disabling MFA is a security-weakening action that creates vulnerability to credential-based attacks. Per CIS Controls 6.5, MFA is required for externally exposed applications. Disabling it violates PCI-DSS 8.3.10, ISO 27001 A.8.5, and SOC 2 CC6.6. This MUST NOT be auto-executed — always requires human approval. Re-enabling via IdP admin console restores the protection.
source_reference: PCI-DSS v4 8.3.10 | CIS Controls v8 6.5 | ISO 27001:2022 A.8.5 | SOC 2 CC6.6
risk_if_not_reversed: Account is vulnerable to credential stuffing, phishing-based takeover, and unauthorized access without second factor

reversal_steps: Re-enable USB storage via GPO: Computer Configuration → Administrative Templates → System → Removable Storage Access
Or via EDR policy (CrowdStrike USB device control)
reversal_basis: USB storage restriction is enforced via Windows Group Policy or EDR device control policies. Disabling USB blocks removable media. Re-enabling via GPO or EDR policy console restores USB access. Business justification required for reversal (e.g., authorized data transfer).
source_reference: CIS Controls v8 10.3 — Disable Autorun and Autoplay for Removable Media | NIST 800-53 MP-7 Media Use
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — disabling USB is a security hardening measure preventing data exfiltration

reversal_steps: ⚠️ Disabling audit logging requires security team approval — it removes compliance controls
reversal_basis: Audit logging is enabled via OS/cloud configuration (auditd, CloudTrail, Azure Monitor). Enabling is a hardening measure that creates no data loss risk. Disabling after the fact is a compliance violation for PCI-DSS (10.2), HIPAA (§164.312(b)), and NIST 800-53 (AU-12). Disabling requires explicit security team authorization.
source_reference: PCI-DSS v4 10.2 | HIPAA §164.312(b) | NIST 800-53 AU-12 Audit Record Generation | CIS Controls v8 8.1
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — enabling audit logging is a compliance hardening measure
